pageCache.text:
SEND Information
SEND - Special Educational Needs & Disability Information
Our school’s shared vision statement values the individuality of all of our children. We are committed to giving all of our children every opportunity to achieve the highest of standards. We do this by taking account of pupils’ varied life experiences and needs.
We offer a broad and balanced curriculum and have high expectations for all children. The achievements, attitudes and well-being of all our children matter. This policy helps to ensure that this federation promotes the individuality of all our children, irrespective of ethnicity, attainment, age, disability, gender or background.
Please write a brief message which will be forwarded directly to Mrs Rogers, who will contact you as soon as she can. Thankyou.

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast Club and The HUB - Wyke Regis Primary Federation
pageCache.text:
WRAP AROUND CARE
BREAKFAST CLUB & THE HUB
Breakfast Club
NEW FOR SPRING 2024 - WRAP AROUND CARE NOW AVAILABLE FOR NURSERY CHILDREN! Our popular Breakfast and After School Clubs are now available for Nursery children to attend. The children are looked after in the Nursery class by familiar staff alongside other Foundation Stage children. This means it is less overwhelming for them and there is no transition to or from the classroom at the beginning and/or end of the day.
Breakfast Club is available to all children who attend the Infant or Junior School from Nursery to Year 6 and is open throughout the school year, term time only. We have been running since September 2012 and are very proud of the service we offer. We are always looking at ways to improve and welcome comments and suggestions from you.
This page provides you with information about what goes on at our Club, as well as forms that can be downloaded.
For those of you who have not made use of our Club yet, please take a look at our leaflet which can be accessed on this page, to see what we offer. In response to requests from parents we have extended our hours and Breakfast Club is now open from 7:15am. We have also reduced rates for children eligible for the Pupil Premium funded sessions.
We hope you find this page useful – if you have any questions about us, please contact either of the school offices or speak to Sam, our Breakfast Club Leader.
The financial and administrative arrangements of the Breakfast Club are dealt with, and managed by, the Infant School. Completed contract and contact/medical forms can be downloaded from the website by clicking on the purple button, completed and then handed to the Infant School Office. Once we have received your paperwork we can then set you up on our cashless payment system which will allow you to book and pay for all sessions online.
We do ask that payment is made in advance. The Infant School can also take payment via the Tax-Free Childcare scheme through the government. Click here for more information.
The Federation runs a daily breakfast club from 7.15am – 8.30am every morning and it is based at the Infant site. Your child will find a welcoming and safe environment along with a healthy breakfast and lots of fun activities. The charge is £5 per session or a reduced rate of £2 per session for Pupil Premium children.
Booking in advance is required to ensure an appropriate staff: pupil ratio is maintained. Please contact the Infant School office on 01305 782470 if you have any further queries.
Breakfast Club Staff
The HUB
As part of the Governing Body’s desire to increase the extended school services provision, we opened our After School Club
“The Hub” (as named by the children) complements the Breakfast Club extending the provision of safe and friendly childcare in familiar surroundings. Sessions run during term time, providing activities and games that engage and stimulate children of different ages. The activities available to children include board games, art and craft activities, books, construction toys, supervised use of technology or the opportunity to complete homework. There is of course also the opportunity to use the school grounds for outdoor play and activities (weather permitting).
The financial and administrative arrangements are managed through the Junior School via an online payment and booking system (Arbor). To register with The Hub, please download the forms available on this page and forward to the Junior School. Our preferred method of payment is online. The Junior School can also take payment via the Tax-Free Childcare scheme through the government. Click here for more information.
As referenced earlier you can make bookings/payments online through the Federation online payment system, Arbor. Pupil Premium rate is available upon request.
“The Hub” session times are:
3.00pm — 4.30pm £6 (£3 for pupil premium)
3.00pm — 5.45pm £12 (£6 for pupil premium)
Booking in advance is required to ensure that an appropriate staff : pupil ratio is maintained. We regret that we are unable to accept same day booking.
Please contact the Junior School office on 01305 786041 should you have any further queries.
The HUB Staff

CLUBS
FEDERATION
Clubs
The Federation prides itself in offering a wide variety of extra-curricular activities including: Choir, Football, Netball, Forest School, First Aid, Cricket, Athletics, Rugby, Hockey, Mindfulness, Art, Rugby, Lego, Computing, Cooking and many others.
These take place at lunchtimes or after school. Any special arrangements with regard to transport to and from home are the responsibility of parents.
After school clubs usually finish by 4pm or 4.15 pm. A text will only be sent home if a club needs to be cancelled at short notice on the day.
Clubs usually run termly, and information on the available clubs and request forms will be sent out at the beginning of each term. You will be notified if your child has a place. Please note, clubs are sometimes very popular and oversubscribed so we can’t always guarantee a place.

pageCache.text:
ABOUT US
JUNIOR SCHOOL
About Our School
Wyke Regis CE Junior School is a Voluntary Controlled mixed school providing education to Key Stage 2 children aged between 7 and 11 years. The school is above average in size and has a maximum number of 360 pupils organised into 12 single-aged classes, with three classes per year group. As a voluntary controlled school we have close links with All Saints Church and have developed an ethos built upon the Christian Faith.
Wyke Regis CE Junior School is a member of the Wyke Regis Primary Federation which partners it with Wyke Regis Infant School & Nursery. The schools share one Head of Federation, one Deputy Head of Federation, one Inclusion Officer and one Governing Body. Links have been established with local Secondary schools enabling children to meet future teachers and to visit their new schools.
The school is also a member of the Chesil Education Partnership (CEP) consisting of all the schools and colleges in Weymouth & Portland. The CEP aims to develop opportunities for all learners to develop to their full potential. The school’s catchment area extends from Lanehouse Rocks Road in the north to Rylands Lane in the east and to the boundary with Portland in the south. The majority of the intake is from our partner federation school, Wyke Regis Infant School & Nursery.
The Aims of Our School
As a Church of England school, we have close links with All Saints Church, and we seek to develop a spiritual ethos built upon the Christian Faith.
Ethos Statement & Safeguarding Our Children
Recognising its historic foundation, the school will develop and preserve its religious character in accordance with the principles of the Church of England and in partnership with the church at parish and diocesan level.
The school encourages an understanding of the meaning and significance of faith and promotes Christian values through the experience it offers to all its pupils.
‘The school is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our children’.
Our School Prayer
Lord Bless me now as I go into your world, let me feel your love, experience your forgiveness, and sense your power within me.
Give me your understanding so that I may understand others. Shower upon me your hope, your peace, your joy.
Amen

pageCache.text:
ABOUT US
INFANTS & NURSERY
About our School
Our school is a Community Infant School serving the area of Wyke Regis. The school caters for an age range of three to seven years. The school’s nursery class offers part time nursery education. There are places for up to twenty-six children at each nursery session. Currently each child is offered up to ten sessions a week. All children can access five sessions for free. Some families may be eligible for 10 free sessions (30 hours – please check the gov website for more information). Any sessions beyond the free hours are charged at £12.75 per 3 hour session. The nursery is a self contained unit with its own entrance, a large classroom, a kitchen area, toilets and a secure outdoor play area.
From September 2026, in addition to the nursery, there will be six class bases for the Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 children. We will have two Reception classes, two Year 1 classes, and two Year 2 classes. Each base has a classroom, an annexe for small group activities, and a large art and craft area. All classes have an outside play area as well as sharing extensive grassed and hard surface play areas.
The school’s accommodation also includes a large hall and library. We have a number of other rooms that we use for small group and individual sessions when required. Each class base contains a small ICT suite.
Since September 2010 the school has federated with Wyke Regis C E Junior School and Mrs Wanda Roberts is the Head of the Federation. The two sites are linked by a path between our school playgrounds.
Since September 2024, we have incorporated an SEMH unit within the school. Places are allocated by a board, on application. Mr Davidson is the lead teacher.
The Aims of Our School
The Wyke Regis Primary Federation promotes high achievement and learning for life by working with children to:
•Develop high self-esteem •Respect themselves and others •Care for the environment •Attain high standards in all areas of learning •Communicate effectively •Enjoy learning •Develop enquiring minds and a spirit of curiosity •Be creative and take risks •Be able to work independently and collaboratively •Understand how well they are doing and how they can continue to improve
We believe that every child will succeed through experiencing quality in:
•A stimulating learning environment •A broad and challenging curriculum •Innovative teaching and an investigative approach to learning •An ethos of support, challenge and encouragement to succeed •Rewarding effort and celebrating achievement •Promoting inclusivity, equality of opportunity and mutual respect •Providing learning partnerships between schools, home and the community
We demonstrate our commitment to working as a learning community by:
•Striving for continuous improvement in all that we do •Working collaboratively towards common goals •Respecting and taking into account the views and opinions of stakeholders •Understanding the part that we all have to play in the success of our federation and its members
Our shared vision is a statement of what we are seeking to achieve. It stimulates, guides and focuses the work of our federation.
Ethos Statement & Safeguarding Our Children
Wyke Regis Primary Federation Developing caring, independent learners for the world community
‘The school is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our children’.

FEDERATION
School Admissions
Dorset LA is the Admissions Authority for our school. From September 2024, the school has a planned admission number (PAN) of 60 children. Where all parental preferences for places at the school can be satisfied, all children seeking a place will be admitted. Where there are too few places available to satisfy all preferences, places will be allocated according to the following priority order:
Parents considering applying to our school are invited to make an appointment to meet the Head of School and view the school premises. Children are very welcome to accompany their parents on this visit. The school premises enables disabled access to all parts of the building and we have a disabled toilet in our administration block. For further information concerning admissions, please contact the school office.
Children are eligible to start the Nursery in the term after they are 3 years old. Children can attend the Nursery for up to ten, 3 hour sessions a week.
Please click here to go to the Nursery page.
Children may start school in the Reception year at the beginning of the school year in which they are five (the school year is from the 1st September to the 31st August). The children starting in Reception will attend on a full time basis of five days a week.
During Year 2, parents will be required to make an application for admission to Junior school.
Admission to Wyke Regis CE Junior School is not automatic; applications must therefore be submitted.
There is close co-operation between the two schools. The children visit the Junior School before the end of the summer term so that they are familiar with their future school and are confident about the new term.

CHRISTIAN VALUES & SIAMS
Federation
Christian Values
Christian Values are at the heart of the school and so children grow and develop in all areas with great strengths in relationships, emotional health and care for each other.
Recognising and valuing the diverse experiences and backgrounds of all children, caring, nurturing and enthusiastic staff work hard to enable them to achieve well.
Challenge and support are given to pupils to enable the to develop in faith and spirituality, thereby understanding what it is to be a member of the wider Christian family.
SIAMS Inspection Report 2024 – Click on our logo above to see report
Inspiring Hearts and Minds
The Wyke Regis Primary Federation promotes high achievement and learning for life by working with children to:
• Develop high self-esteem – as a result of being valued and celebrated
• Respect themselves and others – through collective worship, PSHE and the RE curriculum
• Care for the environment – through a curriculum that enables thought and reflection
• Attain high standards in all areas of learning – as a result of high quality teaching and expectations
• Communicate effectively – by having the opportunity to be involved as stakeholders
• Enjoy learning – through an exciting stimulating curriculum
• Develop enquiring minds and a spirit of curiosity – by listening, watching and reflecting
• Be creative and take risks – by engaging in new experiences and having responsibility
• Be able to work independently and collaboratively – by sharing and caring
• Understand how well they are doing and how they can continue to improve – by giving feedback and support in the learning process
These broad aims are of prime importance to the development of our pupils.

WYKE REGIS PRIMARY FEDERATION
Governing Body
Federation Governors
Welcome to the page detailing the Governors of Wyke Regis Primary Federation, Governors are responsible for overseeing the management side of a school: strategy, policy, budgeting and staffing. They enable their school to run as effectively as possible, working alongside senior leaders (who are responsible for running the school day to day) and supporting teachers to provide excellent education to children.
As Chair of the Governing Body at Wyke Regis Federation I lead a dedicated governing body who are all committed to working with the school senior leadership team and all school staff to ensure our schools deliver the best possible education to the children, in a safe, supportive and welcoming environment here in the heart of the local community in Wyke Regis.
I have a long association with the Federation … back to the 1930’s! My father, my wife and I myself all attended the junior school and my two children attended both the Infant and Junior Schools. Living as close to the school as I do, I have literally seen it just about every day of my life.
The framework and constraints that schools operate under in the 2020’s is challenging to say the least, there are tough performance requirements, very tight financial constraints (made worse by cost of living pressures and large inflationary rises we are all facing) and more children than ever needing additional support.
The task ahead remains tough, but I am convinced that if staff, senior leadership, governors, parents and friends of the federation all work together and keep the children and their education at the heart of all we do, the tasks ahead will be easier to achieve.
I always welcome the opportunity to meet and chat with parents, please do stop and talk to me if you see me around the schools. If in the meantime you need to speak to me, or make me aware of something, you can contact me via the school office(s) or by email.

HOME LEARNING
Brilliant Websites
Mathletics - Love Learning
Mathletics is a web-based learning program which can be used by pupils aged 5 – 18. Mathletics can be used to consolidate learning, practice skills and assess pupil progress.
Pupils have the opportunity to earn credits and points by completing Maths activities and competing against pupils from around the world. Each pupil has a unique user name and the Class Teacher can set specific challenges and activities for individuals and groups.
Mathletics also provides step by step animated support for all mathematical concepts – these can be used on an interactive whiteboard to introduce a topic or by pupils to reinforce learning. Mathletics links to an impressive range of international curriculums including Wales, England, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
Click to Log-in
Times Tables Rock Stars
In either paper form or online, Times Tables Rock Stars is a carefully sequenced programme of daily times tables practice.
Each week concentrates on a different times table, with a recommended consolidation week for rehearsing the tables that have recently been practised every third week or so.
This format has very successfully boosted times tables recall speed for hundreds of thousands of pupils over the last 8 years in over 14,000 schools – both primary and secondary – worldwide.

SAFEGUARDING
FEDERATION
Safeguarding
Safeguarding is the responsibility of all at Wyke Regis Primary Federation.
The dedicated staff of Wyke Regis Federation have regular training in relation to both Special Educational Needs and Safeguarding / Child protection. If you have any concerns please do not hesitate to contact Mrs Roberts (Head of Federation) or any of the Safeguarding team below who will be happy to help.
If you have a concern, inform the designated safeguarding leads as soon as possible. If you are not happy with their decision, you need to make it clear to the team again. If you are still not happy then it is your responsibility to contact Social Care by ringing the following numbers.
As a member of the public, you can ask for advice or refer a concern to the Multi-Agency Safeguarding Hub (MASH) yourself: Tel 01202 228866.
If you have any concerns about a staff member, contact the Senior Leadership Team if appropriate, or the Local Area Designated Officer (LADO) at Dorset County Council. Tel: 01305 228327
SPEAK TO US – WE’RE HERE TO HELP AND TO LISTEN
Our Safeguarding Team
The ‘Prevent’ Strategy
Prevent is about safeguarding people and communities from the threat of terrorism.
You may have heard about the Government’s ‘Prevent’ strategy which covers all types of terrorism and extremism, including the extreme right wing, violent Islamist groups and other causes.
From July 2015 all schools (as well as other organisations) have a duty to safeguard children from radicalisation and extremism. This page is designed to provide parents with information about the strategy and what we are doing as a school to respond to this strategy.
